title: Docs & SOPs — User Manual
summary: How Collections, document types, the WYSIWYG editor, and search work in Docs & SOPs.

sections.body:
Overview

Docs & SOPs is the internal knowledge base for manuals, standard operating procedures, runbooks, checklists, policies, and training material — including this document. Every document belongs to exactly one Collection (this manual, for example, lives in "Asset Register SOPs").

Key Features

  • Library view — a Netflix-style set of shelves (Recently Updated, Review Due Soon, one per Collection, one per document type) with book-style cards that flip on hover to show a summary.
  • List view — a sortable, filterable table for power users.
  • 8 document types, each with its own structured layout: Standard Operating Procedure, Work Instruction, Technical Runbook, Maintenance Checklist, Policy, Show / Production Document, Training Material, General Document.
  • A WYSIWYG rich-text editor (bold/italic/headings/lists/quotes/links/inline images) for every free-text section.
  • Full-text search across titles, tags, and section content (HTML formatting is stripped before indexing, so search matches real words, not markup).
  • File attachments per document, and an optional "Review Due Date" that flags a document once it's overdue.

Step-by-Step

  1. Click New Document, choose a Document Type, then choose a Collection — use Manage next to the Collection field to create a new one if needed.
  2. Fill in the type-specific sections using the rich-text editor toolbar for formatting and inline images.
  3. Set Category, Tags, and (optionally) a Review Due Date, then click Create Document.
  4. To find something later, use the search box or the Type / Category / Collection filters, or just browse the Library shelves.
  5. Open a document and use Add Attachment to attach supporting files.

Tips

  • A document's Document Type can't be changed after creation (it determines its section layout) — its Collection can be changed at any time.
  • Keep this manual and its siblings up to date: whenever a feature described here changes, update the matching document in the "Asset Register SOPs" collection.
